title: T20 World Cup: Two-time champions England survive huge Nepal scare in last-ball thriller
content:
Two-time champions England survived a huge scare to edge out Nepal in a thrilling opening group game in the men’s T20 World Cup.

A dramatic match in the Indian city of Mumbai went down to the final delivery, with Nepal needing to hit a six off it to win, but Sam Curran held his nerve to limit the big-hitting Lokesh Bam to a single, and spare England what would have been an embarrassing defeat.

England captain Harry Brook won the toss and decided his team would bat first. They posted 184, Jacob Bethell top-scoring with 55 from 35 balls faced and Brook making 53 from 32.

A late flurry from Will Jacks, who hit an unbeaten 39 off 18, including three of his four sixes in the final over, had appeared to put England into a strong position. However, Nepal’s reply started with opener Khushal Bhurtel making a quickfire 29 off 17 deliveries, before captain Rohit Paudel made 39 and Dipendra Singh Airee top-scored with an impressive 44 off 29.

Nepal had reached 123-2 before losing wickets, only for the aptly-named Bam to arrive at the crease and put his side within sight once more as he clobbered two sixes off Jofra Archer in the 18th over. But with 10 needed from Curran’s last over, the Surrey all-rounder bowled superbly to ensure a four-run win. Bam ended with 39 off 20 balls.

It will come as a huge relief to Brook and head coach Brendon McCullum, who are hoping for a successful tournament to ease the pressure on England’s setup after a dire Ashes tour earlier this winter and focus on players’ off-field conduct.

The result sets up an intriguing Group C, which also contains West Indies, who won this tournament in 2012 and 2016, and Scotland — who have replaced Bangladesh in the tournament after their withdrawal.

Debutants Italy complete the group, becoming the 25th different national team to feature at a men’s T20 World Cup.

Stuart Law has told his Nepal players he would prefer it if they could shed their nickname of the ‘cardiac kids’ earned because of their propensity for providing nail-biting finishes.

But a dramatic and nerve-racking four-run defeat in Mumbai will have done nothing for the blood pressure of a Nepal coach who came agonisingly close to overseeing one of the World Cup’s greatest upsets.

It was at the last T20 World Cup two years ago that Law was in charge of the United States team who defeated Pakistan and went on to reach the Super Eights.

This would have been an even greater shock because England are widely fancied to win this tournament and add a third T20 title at Ahmedabad on March 8.

How close Nepal came at the Wankhede Stadium and what a demonstration this was of the ability that has made them the fastest growing cricket nation in the world.

Law told The Athletic before the tournament that one of his greatest challenges is managing expectations in cricket-mad Nepal, saying “there will be people calling for my head if we don’t win this World Cup.” And he was only half-joking.

Yet Nepal, who lost to South Africa by just one run in that last T20 World Cup, deserve nothing but praise for taking England so close and showed that their minimum aim of reaching the Super Eights by finishing in the top two in their group is entirely realistic.

This was another good advertisement for a 20-team World Cup and continued an excellent start to this tournament by joining the Netherlands, Scotland, USA and Afghanistan in pushing more celebrated opponents to the brink over the opening weekend.
